svg.desc: Escape response of a focal group of 18 Grevy's zebra (*Equus grevyi*) filmed from overhead drones at the Mpala Conservancy, Kenya. (a) Georeferenced trajectories of the 18 tracked zebra on the aerial orthomosaic of the grazing site: the focal animal of this panel in black, the rest of the group in white, with the focal animal's body orientation every 5 m of straight-line travel as arrows (orange before the approach stimulus, purple after). The circular insets (orange / purple) magnify the moments indicated by each callout and show the body-heading arrow drawn at that moment. (b) A Grevy's zebra. (c) Posterior distribution of the equally weighted mean direction of the 18 focal zebras before and after the approach: the loop traces the relative density of the group-mean-direction posterior draws (radial scale 0 to 1) and the marker the posterior mean direction. (d) Group-level alignment: the resultant length of the 18 fitted individual mean directions, with the posterior mean before and after the approach. (e) Individual-level mean directions: the posterior density of each fitted individual mean direction (loops) and each animal's observed circular-mean heading (markers). (f) Individual-level concentration: each animal's posterior mean resultant length with 95% HDI, before and after the approach, paired within animal across conditions. Panels c-f are evaluated from a saved hierarchical von Mises fit of the block-averaged body orientations (4 chains x 1,000 draws, zero divergent transitions); the 'group' in c-d is the finite focal group, not a population parameter.
svg.title: Zebra escape response
